_comment: Out of Africa: dated sites with remains or traces of Homo sapiens (the Captain, 11 Oct 2026). Each date is the one its Wikipedia article gives; disputes are noted. The globe draws the area around every site reached by the moment shown — where the evidence is, not a boundary of where people lived. src/components/migration.ts

sites.name: Jebel Irhoud
sites.note: The oldest known Homo sapiens remains: a weighted average age of 315,000 years (2017) — modern humans were already across Africa.

sites.name: Misliya Cave
sites.note: Among the oldest Homo sapiens remains outside Africa, dated to 185,000 years ago.

sites.name: Skhul and Qafzeh
sites.note: Modern humans in the Levant c. 100,000–80,000 years ago (thermoluminescence and ESR dating).

sites.name: Madjedbebe
sites.note: Occupied possibly by 65,000 ± 6,000 years ago (2017) and at least by 50,000; the older date is questioned by some experts.

sites.name: Ust'-Ishim
sites.note: A thighbone radiocarbon-dated to 45,000 years ago — at the time the oldest directly dated modern human.

sites.name: Bacho Kiro Cave
sites.note: Some of Europe's earliest modern humans, 44,000–40,000 years ago, with recent Neanderthal ancestors.

sites.name: Tianyuan Cave
sites.note: Bones radiocarbon-dated to 42,000–39,000 years ago. Placed at the nearby Zhoukoudian site (the cave is about 6 km away).

sites.name: Lake Mungo
sites.note: Mungo Man, about 40,000 years old — the oldest Homo sapiens remains in Australia.

sites.name: White Sands footprints
sites.note: Human footprints dated 23,000–21,000 years ago by seeds in the layers (2021); the long-held consensus put arrival in the Americas at 13,000–16,000 years ago.

sites.name: Monte Verde
sites.note: Monte Verde II, generally dated to 14,500 years ago — though a 2026 study argues the campsite is no older than 8,200 years.
